title: Odile and the Winter
premise: Felix Montrose arrives at Blackfen School to teach the children no one else will, in a village where a class goes missing every winter and everyone politely forgets. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the school's foundations, Felix discovers the missing students were never taken—they chose to leave, joining a family that has lived below since before the village existed and now demands its tithe of children to keep its count whole. As the winter count approaches, Felix must descend into the family's halls, win back the trust of her vanished students, and break the bargain that binds them—learning that justice outside the law sometimes means freeing people from a debt they never agreed to pay. In the end she brings most of the family's captives into the light, but one child chooses to stay below, and Felix must live with a door that closes on her own terms.
about_author: Yara Pemberton is a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in northern villages where old bargains still shape daily life. She writes horror about institutions, memory, and the quiet violence of belonging.

chapters.title: The Roster
chapters.summary: Felix Montrose arrives at Blackfen School with a class list that doesn't match the empty desks. POV: Felix. The headmaster, Mr. Aldous, hands her a register with names crossed out in pencil, never ink. Emotional beat: wary professionalism masking unease as the village's polite silences begin to register.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Desks
chapters.summary: Felix teaches her first week; the children are bright but flinch at the word 'winter.' POV: Felix. A girl named Ivetta corrects Felix's lesson on local history, describing a family under the hill as if reciting scripture. Emotional beat: creeping wrongness beneath ordinary routine.

chapters.title: What the Village Forgets
chapters.summary: Felix interviews parents about last year's missing class; every answer is warm, vague, and identical. POV: Felix. The pub landlord offers her tea instead of answers, then warns her not to dig. Emotional beat: isolation—the first sense that forgetting here is enforced, not natural.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: A county crew begins digging a drainage trench behind the school despite Aldous's objections. POV: Felix. She watches from her classroom window as students press their palms to the glass, watching the machines like mourners. Emotional beat: dread gathering at the edges of civic normalcy.

chapters.title: Sealed From Inside
chapters.summary: The crew unearths a stone door, bolted shut from within, carved with tally marks older than the village. POV: alternating Felix and the foreman, Dree. Dree touches the marks and counts aloud without meaning to. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear; the past asserting itself.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Absence
chapters.summary: Three students don't come to class. Their beds are made, their shoes left neatly by doors. POV: Felix. Aldous files the absences without comment, and the constable refuses to open a case. Emotional beat: fury at institutional indifference; Felix resolves to investigate alone.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Felix finds the tally marks on the door match the number of missing students across decades—and the count is incomplete. POV: Felix. In the archive she learns the village pays a 'winter count' of children to something it calls only the Family. Emotional beat: horror reframed as bookkeeping; injustice taking shape.

chapters.title: Ivetta's Window
chapters.summary: Ivetta appears at Felix's lodgings at night, half-frozen, saying she ran from below because they asked her to bring her brother next. POV: Ivetta. She describes the Family's halls: warm, lit, full of children who smile too readily. Emotional beat: terror mixed with terrible temptation.

chapters.title: Aldous Confesses
chapters.summary: Confronted, Aldous admits he was a counted child who was returned when his sister took his place. POV: Aldous. He begs Felix to let the count finish, insisting the alternative is worse. Emotional beat: grief and complicity; the law's failure laid bare.

chapters.title: The Door Opens
chapters.summary: The excavated door unlocks itself overnight; cold air flows out, smelling of bread and beeswax. POV: Felix. Footprints lead down, small ones, and the remaining students grow restless, drawn toward the stairwell. Emotional beat: threshold dread; the story tips from mystery to descent.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Felix follows the footprints into the Family's halls, leaving chalk arrows behind her. POV: Felix. She finds classrooms below—older, better lit than hers—where missing students are taught willingly by gentle, wrong-faced elders. Emotional beat: disorientation; the enemy is hospitable.

chapters.title: The Family's Argument
chapters.summary: The Family's matriarch, Mother Sallow, explains the bargain: the village founded itself on land owed to those beneath, and the count is rent. POV: Felix. Sallow insists the children are happier below, and some evidence agrees. Emotional beat: moral vertigo—justice looks different from underneath.

chapters.title: Chalk Arrows Washed Away
chapters.summary: Felix tries to lead three students out; two turn back at the threshold, and her chalk marks have been erased. POV: Felix. Above ground, Ivetta waits all night at the sealed hatch. Emotional beat: heartbreak; you cannot rescue people who believe they belong elsewhere.

chapters.title: Memory Below
chapters.summary: In the lower halls Felix finds a room of ledgers recording every counted child, including her own name, entered years before she arrived. POV: Felix. Her invisibility was arranged; she was always meant to be the final entry. Emotional beat: violation and revelation—her belonging was stolen twice.

chapters.title: The Returned Ones
chapters.summary: Felix seeks out adults like Aldous who came back, finding them hollowed, unable to remember their own mothers' faces. POV: Felix and returned villager Tam Wicke. Tam remembers only warmth, and weeps without knowing why. Emotional beat: pity sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Breaking the Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix steals the ledger and burns it in the school stove; the count collapses into arithmetic without authority. POV: Felix. The village wakes to remember, all at once, every name it surrendered. Emotional beat: catharsis and chaos—justice delivered outside any court.

chapters.title: Mother Sallow's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Sallow descends on the school during assembly, demanding restitution for the burned record. POV: alternating Felix and Sallow. The villagers, remembering, stand between her and the children—an entire town finally refusing its debt. Emotional beat: confrontation; collective courage against ancient claim.

chapters.title: The Bargain Rewritten
chapters.summary: Felix offers a new terms: the Family may teach any child who freely chooses to stay, but none will be counted, taken, or forgotten. POV: Felix. Sallow, bound by the logic of consent she herself invoked, accepts. Emotional beat: hard-won negotiation; freedom framed as choice, not rescue.

chapters.title: Those Who Stay
chapters.summary: The freed children surface into daylight; most run to their parents, but one boy, Pell, turns back down the stairs. POV: Pell. He kisses his mother's hand and says he learned everything he loves below. Emotional beat: bittersweet cost of true freedom.

chapters.title: Spring Count
chapters.summary: Spring comes; Felix reopens school with a full, honest roster and a new rule: every absence gets investigated, every name gets remembered. POV: Felix. The village holds its first memorial for the counted dead. Emotional beat: mourning and repair; memory reclaimed as institution.

chapters.title: The Door Ajar
chapters.summary: Felix visits the excavation site monthly; the door stands unlocked now, and sometimes warm light spills up the stairs. POV: Felix. Once, she hears children laughing below, and does not intervene. Emotional beat: uneasy peace; coexistence over conquest.

chapters.title: Register of Names
chapters.summary: Years later, Felix compiles a public register of every child ever counted, read aloud each winter solstice. POV: Felix, closing frame. The final line belongs to Pell, grown, visiting from below with his own students. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than imposed; the winter ends, but is honored.
